topics.flagship-ru-ua: Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre in Zaporizhia, killing at least 31 people according to the regional head, who called it one of the deadliest attacks there since the full-scale invasion began. Both Ukraine and Russia say their air raid alert apps were hacked. Zelenskyy told Fox News Ukraine will keep striking Russian oil refineries unless Trump supplies Patriot missiles, Russia confirmed peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week, and Merz doubts Moscow is serious about a truce. A single-source Kyiv Independent tally reportedly puts civilian deaths from Russian strikes on Oct. 29-30 at 27, including 15 at a Dnipro train station.
topics.flagship-ir-il: The US struck Qeshm Island, its first attack there since June, while Iranian President Pezeshkian signalled more diplomacy. Qatari mediators visited Tehran, and the US and Iran are weighing mediators' proposals amid limited airstrikes. A US official said the US carried out defensive strikes on Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz. US and Gulf officials are reportedly sceptical of Israeli warnings about Iranian chemical weapon delivery. Single-source items include Iranian tunnel footage, a former CIA officer's claim that Trump is considering a nuclear strike (unverified), and intensifying Houthi-government fighting near Taiz.
topics.T15: Flash flooding forced polling place changes in seven Florida counties on Election Day. Separate single-source reports describe evacuation orders from flooding in the US Southwest and a cyclone expected to make landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast with winds up to 120 kmph. The remaining items concern preparedness, including a Philippine earthquake and tsunami drill, Canada's three-day emergency supply advice, and flood insurance costs.
topics.T01: Single-source reports describe Myanmar junta airstrikes in Rakhine State: one destroyed a bridge in Kyauktaw and killed seven civilians, and another damaged an MSF-supported maternity ward in Mrauk-U and reportedly killed five, including a newborn. Sudan is demanding UN accountability over RSF drone attacks that have strained its relations with Ethiopia. Politico reportedly says NATO fears reduced US involvement if Republicans lose the midterms.
topics.T02: Sources are sparse and limited to single outlets. The UN says more than 13,000 pregnant women in Yemen's Taiz have lost access to essential healthcare because of fighting and blocked routes. Other reports cover displaced Sudanese returning to Khartoum, MSF mental health support in Sudan, and a UNICEF nutrition workshop in Benue, Nigeria.
topics.T03: A Quincy, Illinois man accused of mailing fake anthrax letters to Illinois lawmakers will remain jailed ahead of his Dec. 7 federal trial. This is the only item under the topic.
topics.T04: An anthrax outbreak has killed 30 hippos in Virunga National Park, DR Congo, since September. Kenya discharged five recovered Ebola patients and released 46 contacts from quarantine, and Nigeria is reportedly facing an unidentified illness with about 30 deaths in Zamfara, with speculation about Ebola but no official confirmation. New York reported its first measles death in over 30 years after declaring a state of emergency. Other reports cover a campus waterborne outbreak in Odisha, a warning about an 'unprecedented' outbreak, and an influenza stockpiling modeling study.
topics.T05: Belgian PM Bart De Wever submitted his resignation after budget talks failed, and the king is weighing whether to accept it. In Poland, the Constitutional Tribunal is meeting on its future after its president was suspended in a dispute with the government, which some outlets frame as a power struggle between Tusk and Nawrocki. Other items are commentary on Cuba and the UK Palestine Action group.
topics.T06: German officials blamed left-wing groups and 'migrant troublemakers' for weekend rioting and looting, and France is bracing for renewed student protests. Reports tie Spain's Barcelona riots to a French-inspired movement. Dockworkers at 113 ports reportedly staged a coordinated strike over Israeli and US military cargo, and Iran reportedly executed two more political prisoners from the January uprising. The Henry Nowak case in the UK also drew political controversy over related riots.
topics.T08: Single-source reports describe Indian navy commandos rescuing 20 crew from an Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia, amid a resurgence of piracy. Two Colombian soldiers were killed in an explosive drone attack in Choco, with the ELN suspected. Jordan filed terrorism charges over the Oct. 23 attack on a church in Karak. Other items cover an alleged TTP figure killed in a Pakistani airstrike in Kandahar, banditry politics in Nigeria, and terror-financing raids in Srinagar.
topics.T10: Items are single-source and loosely related. Cyprus is reportedly phasing out Russian weapons and expanding defense cooperation with the US. Germany's Stark Defence plans a 24-meter uncrewed surface vessel next year to hunt Russia's shadow fleet. Erdogan is in South Korea reportedly seeking nuclear collaboration, and UK Defence Secretary Streeting says he is confident of hitting the defense spending target.
topics.T11: US and Indian forces began the Tiger Triumph 2026 exercise in Visakhapatnam, focused on humanitarian assistance and disaster response. The Royal Navy intercepted a Russian spy ship monitoring NATO exercises off Scotland. INS Sahyadri concluded a naval exercise in Busan with South Korea, and India and Australia concluded AUSTRAHIND 2026 in Kerala.
topics.T12: Britain's cyberchief says the UK is likely to face AI-enabled cyberattacks on critical infrastructure by 2028, and a cyberattack on cold stores in supermarkets across Europe has no clear culprit. North Korea denies US allegations that it was behind a $6 billion Binance crypto heist. Thai opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut was reportedly targeted with spyware, and hackers reportedly hijacked Ukraine's emergency alert system to broadcast a false nuclear alert. One item is corrupted and unreadable.
topics.T13: Reporting is sparse and mostly political commentary from single outlets. Ceuta is seeking a 2027 'war budget' after a mass migrant entry in late July. Farage vowed to revoke citizenship from some migrants, and a former Biden-era Border Patrol chief said the US border has never been this quiet.
topics.T14: The US Embassy in Moscow warned in October of a possible mass-casualty event at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, and Russia's FSB then detained a teenager allegedly planning an attack. The US Embassy in Saudi Arabia issued an alert about possible Houthi attacks and airport disruptions in Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam. Police in London arrested about 320 Palestine Action supporters protesting outside the US Embassy.
topics.T16: US midterm elections are underway on Nov. 3, with control of Congress at stake and Democrats favored by oddsmakers and polls. Attention is on Michigan's Senate race, where Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed. Flooding forced polling place changes in seven Florida counties, and commentary links the results to US policy on Ukraine, Iran and NATO.

bluf: Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre in Zaporizhia, killing at least 31 people according to Ukraine's regional head, who called it one of the deadliest attacks there since the full-scale invasion began. Britain's cyberchief says the UK is likely to face AI-enabled cyberattacks on critical infrastructure by 2028. A cyberattack has hit cold stores in supermarkets across Europe, and no culprit has been identified. An anthrax outbreak has killed 30 hippos in DR Congo's Virunga National Park since September. Ukraine and Russia both say their air raid alert apps were hacked, and hackers reportedly broadcast a false nuclear alert across Ukraine. Separately, the US struck Qeshm Island, its first attack there since June, and a US official said it also carried out defensive strikes in the Strait of Hormuz, while Qatari mediators held talks in Tehran. Russia confirmed Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week, though Merz doubts Moscow is serious about a truce. Belgian PM Bart De Wever submitted his resignation after budget talks failed, and the king is weighing whether to accept it.
